title: How Can One Attain Rebirth?
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Question: How can one be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss?

inline.s: Ten recitations at life's end, continued without interruption, bring rebirth at once.
The first thing a Buddha-reciter must be clear about is:
How can one attain rebirth?
Otherwise one will head south while the cart points north,
and ruin the great matter of one's own rebirth.
Question: How can one be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss?
Answer: How one can be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss — this is the Pure Land school's
core
It determines how the teaching masters should instruct and how students should practice,
so as to ensure rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss
On this point, Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, Master Shandao, and Master Yongming have all given clear instruction.
Master Tanluan and Master Daochuo were sages who had realized the fruit; Master Shandao and Master Yongming were emanations of Amitabha Buddha. Their words are
the authoritative words of the sages
[The authoritative words of the sages] These are the words of sages — correct, free of error, and certain to be accepted with faith.
Master Tanluan instructs
(for details, see
Master Tanluan's Teaching on the Pure Land Dharma
With no other mind intermingled
(unmixed with wandering thoughts)
, thought following thought in succession
(thought succeeding thought)
, even ten recitations — this is called the ten recitations in uninterrupted succession.
If the ten recitations at life's end continue without interruption, one immediately attains rebirth.
Master Daochuo instructs
(for details, see
Master Daochuo's Teaching on the Pure Land Dharma
If there are beings who, even having committed evil all their lives,
at the moment of death, in ten recitations continuing without interruption
, call upon my name,
if they should not be reborn, I will not attain perfect awakening.
Master Shandao, an emanation of Amitabha Buddha, instructs
(for details, see
Master Shandao's Teaching on the Pure Land Dharma
Continued without interruption, rebirth follows
. If one can
continue thought after thought
until the end of life
then of ten, ten will be reborn; of a hundred, a hundred will be reborn.
If I attain Buddhahood, the beings of the ten directions who call upon my name and wish to be born in my land,
down to ten recitations
(down to ten recitations continuing without interruption at life's end)
, if they should not be reborn, I will not attain perfect awakening.
[Continued without interruption, rebirth follows]

At the moment of death, so long as the thoughts of Buddha-recitation continue without interruption (not broken by wandering thoughts), one immediately attains rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[Down to ten recitations]
The "down to ten recitations" spoken of here, taken together with Master Shandao's instruction quoted above,
"precisely because calling the name is easy, continued without interruption, rebirth follows. If one can
continue thought after thought, until the end of life
, then of ten, ten will be reborn; of a hundred, a hundred will be reborn,"
it is plainly evident that this is
"up to a whole lifetime
(one life)
of thought after thought continuing, and down to
ten recitations continuing without interruption at life's end
stated in abbreviated form, for Master Shandao has already clearly said:
"Continue thought after thought, until the end of life."
And
"continue thought after thought, until the end of life"
is precisely to make the uninterrupted succession of thought become an ingrained habit,
so as to ensure ten recitations continuing without interruption at life's end
If one recites the Buddha's name in ordinary times but does not recite at life's end, or if at life's end one does recite but with a scattered mind, this is not
"continue thought after thought, until the end of life"
. Therefore, the meaning of "down to ten recitations" is
"down to the ten recitations continuing without interruption at life's end"
. This rhetorical device of terse, essential expression is found everywhere in classical Chinese. Thus
"down to ten recitations, if they should not be reborn, I will not attain perfect awakening"
means exactly:
Ten recitations at life's end, continued without interruption, bring rebirth at once.
[Ten recitations] Reciting ten utterances of the Buddha's name.
[Continue thought after thought, making it an ingrained habit] Through repeated practice, make the uninterrupted succession of thought into second nature.

Master Shandao was an emanation of Amitabha Buddha, and his words are the words of Amitabha Buddha. How one can attain rebirth must of course be based on his words as the ground of certainty — this is the authoritative word of the sages. Buddha-reciters must engrave this upon their hearts, believing it all the more and relying upon it all the more.

Note: In Master Shandao's time, through the teaching of these three generations of patriarchs — Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao — the fact that ten recitations continuing without interruption at life's end is the condition for rebirth had already become the common understanding of Buddha-reciters of the day, and the barest common knowledge among them.
Therefore
"down to ten recitations, if they should not be reborn, I will not attain perfect awakening"
plainly means:
Ten recitations at life's end, continued without interruption, bring rebirth at once.
Unless one is a complete outsider who understands nothing, or a wicked person who slanders the Dharma with ulterior motives, one would never
distort "down to ten recitations, if they should not be reborn, I will not attain perfect awakening"

into "reciting ten utterances with a scattered mind in ordinary times brings rebirth." This is why Master Shandao employed the terse, essential expression "down to ten recitations," making the whole sentence concise and well-formed, pleasant to read aloud, and easy to memorize and recite.
Moreover, Master Shandao stated it plainly:
"Continued without interruption, rebirth follows. If one can
continue thought after thought, until the end of life
, then of ten, ten will be reborn; of a hundred, a hundred will be reborn.
May all people think this over well; in walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, they must
sharpen the mind and restrain the self
(spur oneself on and discipline oneself)
never ceasing day or night
(never ceasing the uninterrupted succession of thought, day or night)
, so that as the former thought comes to an end, the latter thought brings rebirth at once. Ever enjoying the Dharma-bliss of non-action, even unto Buddhahood — what joy!
(for details, see
Master Shandao's Teaching on the Pure Land Dharma
If "reciting ten utterances with a scattered mind in ordinary times brings rebirth" were so, then why the need for
"continue thought after thought, until the end of life"
? And why the need for
"in walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, you must sharpen the mind and restrain the self, never ceasing day or night"
? Therefore the distortion by Huijing, Jingzong, and others of
"down to ten recitations, if they should not be reborn, I will not attain perfect awakening"
into "reciting ten utterances with a scattered mind in ordinary times brings rebirth" (and their loud advocacy on that basis of "calling the name ensures rebirth") is completely mistaken.
Master Yongming, an emanation of Amitabha Buddha, instructs
The Myriad Good Deeds Returning to the One
The present is the cause, the moment of death is the result
; therefore the cause must be made real, and the result will not be empty. If one wants
the ten recitations at life's end to be accomplished
(if one wants to accomplish the ten recitations continuing without interruption at life's end)
, then
prepare the ford and bridge beforehand
(make full preparation in advance)
, gather together one's merits and virtues, and dedicate them to that time
(dedicate them to the moment of death)
, with every thought not falling short
(with every thought continuing without interruption)
, and there will be no cause for worry.
[Accomplish the ten recitations at life's end] To accomplish the ten recitations continuing without interruption at life's end. (For details, see the article
Ten Recitations at Life's End, Continued Without Interruption, Bring Rebirth at Once

.) [Prepare the ford and bridge beforehand] To make full preparation in advance. "Ford and bridge" means a ferry crossing and a bridge. "Prepare the ford and bridge beforehand" means to make full preparation in advance.
Śākyamuni Buddha instructs
the Buddha's Sūtra of Immeasurable Life
Though there is toil and hardship for one lifetime, in a moment one will be born in the Land of Immeasurable Life, where joy is boundless.
[Conclusion] How can one attain rebirth? The answer:
Ten recitations at life's end, continued without interruption, bring rebirth at once.

Therefore, students must find the concrete method by which they can achieve ten recitations continuing without interruption at life's end, and then practice with unflagging diligence and perseverance; and teaching masters must also teach this concrete method, giving concrete guidance and encouragement.
